html:
Polybius was a Greek historian and statesman who lived from about 200 to 118 BCE. His Histories explain how Rome came to rule the Mediterranean world in barely fifty years.

He came from Megalopolis in the Peloponnese and was a leader of the Achaean League. After Rome beat Macedon at the Battle of Pydna in 168 BCE, he was one of a thousand leading Achaeans taken to Italy as hostages. In Rome he became a close friend of the young Scipio Aemilianus, and he was with him when Rome destroyed Carthage in 146 BCE (Rome destroys Carthage and Corinth). He then helped settle Greek affairs after Rome sacked Corinth the same year.

His Histories, in forty books, covered the years from 264 to 146 BCE, from the First Punic War onward; five survive whole. He travelled to see places himself, used documents, and insisted that history should teach practical lessons. He argued that Rome's strength came from its mixed constitution, a balance of consuls, Senate and people. That idea later influenced Montesquieu and the framers of the United States Constitution.
sum: Polybius was a Greek historian and statesman who lived from about 200 to 118 BCE. His Histories explain how Rome came to rule the Mediterranean world in barely fifty years.
